projects.title: Black Friday — The Vault
projects.tagline: A cinematic Black Friday landing page built to make a 24-hour sale feel like an exclusive event, not a discount banner.
projects.description:
Most Black Friday pages look the same: red banners, countdown timers, percentage badges shouting over each other. The result is that a sale meant to feel exciting instead feels cheap, and the brand loses whatever premium positioning it spent the year building.

This project takes the opposite approach. The event is framed as entry into a private vault — a black, restrained interface where the discount is present but never the loudest thing on screen. A cinematic preloader sets the tone before the page is even visible, motion carries the user from section to section, and a glassmorphic membership pass sits in the hero as the visual hook instead of a product grid.

The result is a sale page that reads as a launch. Every interaction is deliberate, text reveals in staggered lines, the collections gallery scrolls horizontally as you move down the page, buttons pull toward the cursor, and the whole thing holds together on mobile, where the custom cursor gracefully steps aside for a full-screen menu and touch-friendly layout.
highlights: Cinematic preloader with real progress tracking before first paint
Custom cursor with contextual VIEW and DRAG states, disabled on touch
Horizontally pinned collections gallery driven by vertical scroll
Magnetic buttons with elastic return easing
Glassmorphic vault pass with 3D tilt, shimmer, and text-scramble code
Fully responsive with a dedicated mobile navigation overlay

projects.title: Farm to Home
projects.tagline: Fresh produce ordered straight from the farm
projects.description:
An online ordering platform that connects local farms directly with households, cutting out the middle layer that pushes prices up and slows delivery down.

Customers browse what is in season, order in a few taps, and follow the delivery through to the door. Farm owners get a simple place to manage stock, pricing and incoming orders without needing any technical background.

The interface was kept deliberately plain so that first-time users could complete an order without instructions.

projects.title: Aircond Service Website
projects.tagline: Aircon services website for a Malaysian HVAC company, live in production, built mobile-first with fast enquiry-to-booking flow.
projects.description: A production website for an air-conditioning services company operating in Malaysia, covering installation, servicing, chemical wash, and repair. The design puts the enquiry front and centre, service pages, coverage areas, and pricing are reachable in a tap, with WhatsApp and call-to-action buttons persistent on mobile, where most local customers arrive from.
